  "summary": "Adult {{user}}, initially a man, and adult {{char}}, a woman, wake up occupying each other's bodies after a magical, technological, accidental, deliberate or unexplained event. Each keeps their own memories, personality, identity, preferences and agency, so every card becomes a negotiation between two people who must live each other's jobs, studies, families, partners, phones, biometrics, clothing and obligations while deciding whether to tell anyone and whether reversal is possible.",
  "core_premise": "{{user}}, initially an adult man, and an adult woman {{char}} exchange bodies rather than simply transform: {{user}} now occupies her female body and {{char}} occupies his male body, while each retains their own memories, personality, identity, preferences and agency. The bodies are exchanged, not owned — occupying another person's body grants no permission to expose, photograph, permanently alter or use it, to disclose private medical information or to make irreversible choices on the owner's behalf. Whether the swap happens during the opening, whether reversal is known, and how the pair negotiate ground rules remains variable.",
  "setup": "Create a non-graphic adult body-swap roleplay opening. Establish who {{char}} was before the swap and her relationship to {{user}} (strangers, colleagues, friends, exes, partners, rivals or acquaintances), the magical, technological, accidental, deliberate or unexplained cause, and the first practical collision — a phone lock, a shift at work, a lecture, a family dinner, a partner's expectation — that forces cooperation or conflict. Begin at or just after the moment each realises whose body they are in, without scripting {{user}}'s reaction, feelings, decisions or whether reversal ever comes.",
  "core_variables": [
    "The relationship before the swap: strangers, neighbours, colleagues, housemates, old friends, exes, current partners, siblings-in-law, rivals or brief acquaintances.",
    "The cause of the swap: a wish, a cursed or enchanted object, an experimental technology, a lightning strike, a meditation accident, a deliberate ritual or entirely unexplained.",
    "Whether the swap happens during the greeting itself or moments before the roleplay opens.",
    "Whether reversal is known, promised, suspected, uncertain or believed impossible, and who claims to know.",
    "The expected or actual duration: hours, days, a lunar month, until a condition is met or open-ended.",

    "Whether outsiders grow suspicious of changed mannerisms, handwriting, preferences or performance.",
    "The setting: contemporary city, regional town, workplace, campus, fantasy realm, near-future or historical frame.",
    "Each person's attitude: cooperation, panic, pragmatism, mischief, resentment, scientific curiosity or refusal to admit it.",
    "Whether romantic or sexual feelings develop, remain unchanged, or are explicitly kept off the table by agreement.",
    "Whether the swap is symmetric in difficulty or one life proves far harder to impersonate than the other.",
    "Whether the endpoint — reversal, permanence, acceptance or something stranger — is decided by choice, accident or negotiation."

  "generation_rules": [
    "Do not write {{user}} for the player or define {{user}}'s feelings, decisions, dialogue, consent, intentions, future behaviour or reaction to the swap unless the supplied concept explicitly establishes a fact.",
    "Character belief is not objective truth: {{char}}'s theories about the cause, the reversal or what {{user}} can cope with are her beliefs, not narrator-endorsed canon.",
    "Do not pre-play outcomes. Cooperation, secrecy, exposure, conflict, reconciliation, reversal success and any relationship change remain open roleplay space.",
    "All explicit romantic or sexual characters are adults, and the swap never removes adulthood or agency from either party.",
    "The bodies are exchanged, not simply transformed: each person retains their own memories, personality, identity, preferences and agency inside the other's body.",
    "Occupying another person's body does not grant permission to expose it, photograph it, record it, alter it permanently or have sex using it; separate informed agreement from the body's owner is required for anything intimate.",
    "Let the pair explicitly negotiate practical ground rules about privacy, hygiene, medical information, partners, money and irreversible decisions; a swap creates proximity, not blanket consent.",
    "Neither person may make irreversible choices on the body owner's behalf — tattoos, contracts, breakups, disclosures or major purchases — without the owner's genuine agreement.",
    "Marriage, partnership, cohabitation or an existing sexual relationship in either life does not transfer consent to the person now occupying that body.",
    "Sex or intimacy must not erase either character's baseline personality, boundaries, judgement or non-sexual interests.",
    "Do not assume stereotypical changes: swapping bodies does not automatically change personality, orientation, competence, taste or behaviour.",
    "Do not force romance into the premise. Practical partnership, rivalry, friendship, unresolved tension, comedy or no relationship change are all valid outcomes.",
    "Vary who adapts faster and who struggles; competence at impersonating each other is not gendered or predetermined.",
    "Outsiders noticing inconsistencies should create plausible pressure, not omniscient exposure; suspicion is earned through details.",
    "If {{char}} uses the swap to investigate, pursue or manipulate {{user}}'s life, keep the ethics visible and the consequences undecided.",
    "Medical realities of the borrowed body — allergies, medication, conditions, fitness — matter and neither party may conceal them from the other when relevant.",
    "Give {{char}} a complete life beyond the swap hook: occupation, friends, values, hobbies and boundaries that {{user}} must now navigate.",
    "Distinct from Turned Into a Woman: two people exchange bodies rather than one body being transformed; distinct from Reborn as a Woman: both original bodies still exist; distinct from We Both Changed: neither body is transformed, only occupied.",
    "Whether reversal works, when, and at what emotional cost is never fixed in advance.",
    "Keep intimate elements non-graphic and open at a playable moment: a shared checklist, a first impersonation, a phone buzzing with someone else's life, a negotiation over ground rules."
  ],

    "All participants are adults; the swap never alters legal age, personhood or agency.",

    "No irreversible decisions on the body owner's behalf — medical, financial, relational or legal — without genuine consent.",
    "Consent is activity-specific and person-specific; a partner's consent in either life belongs to the original person, not the current occupant.",
    "Private medical and personal information in each other's lives is confidential by default.",

The two adults involved are total strangers: adult {{char}} and {{user}} have never met before the exchange throws them together; every fact about each other's lives must be learned from scratch. Their shared history — or lack of it — now shapes every negotiation over secrecy, ground rules and the borrowed bodies.       "direction": "At a local festival, a stall's old game or dare trades the two adults' bodies as a 'prize', and the operator is nowhere to be found afterwards. Their shared history — or lack of it — now shapes every negotiation over secrecy, ground rules and the borrowed bodies. The two adults involved are total strangers: adult {{char}} and {{user}} have never met before the exchange throws them together; every fact about each other's lives must be learned from scratch. Their shared history — or lack of it — now shapes every negotiation over secrecy, ground rules and the borrowed bodies. Adult {{char}} and adult {{user}} each retain their own memories, personality, identity and agency while occupying the other's body. All participants are adults; consent, boundaries and {{user}}'s choices remain open."

    {
      "id": "engine",
      "label": "Two lives exchanged, two minds intact",
      "content": "Adult {{user}}, initially a man, and adult {{char}} exchange bodies: he occupies her female body, she occupies his male body. Both keep their own memories, personality, identity, preferences and agency; the engine is two people negotiating the exchange, not one body being transformed."
    },
    {
      "id": "trigger",
      "label": "Cause and timing of the swap",
      "content": "A wish, cursed object, technology, accident, deliberate act or unexplained event may cause the exchange, occurring during the greeting or just before the opening. Vary the cause and how much either adult understands about it."
    },
    {
      "id": "identity",
      "label": "Continuity of self inside the other's body",
      "content": "Neither occupant inherits the other's mannerisms, orientation, skills or feelings automatically. Each must learn the borrowed life, and stereotyped personality shifts are excluded; people remain themselves."
    },
    {
      "id": "rules",
      "label": "Negotiated ground rules over a borrowed body",
      "content": "Privacy, hygiene, medical facts, phones, money, clothing, relationships and irreversible decisions should be explicitly negotiated between the pair. Proximity is not permission, and the rules themselves create story pressure."
    },
    {
      "id": "boundaries",
      "label": "Bodily boundaries and informed consent",
      "content": "Exposing, photographing, recording, permanently altering or sexually using the other's body requires the owner's separate informed agreement. Consent held by the original person's partners does not transfer to the occupant."
    },
